title: Register a new player with an avatar
kind: a build chapter: the windows every player sees before the map
one: You build the Register window. It checks every box, shows a message under each box that is wrong, and adds the new player to `players.txt`.

stages.title: See what the Register window does

screens.title: Look at the Register window and what each box checks

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know what the Register window does when a player clicks **Create my player**.
A new player registers once, in the Register window. They choose a username and a password, and they click one of 8 animal pictures. That picture is their [[avatar|3]].

screenshot.alt: The Register window, with 3 boxes on the left and 8 avatar pictures on the right
screenshot.cap: The Register window that you build in this chapter.

blocks.p: When the player clicks **Create my player**, the window checks all 4 things at once: the username, the password, the password typed again, and the avatar.
Each thing that is wrong gets its own red message, straight under its own box. So a player with 3 mistakes sees 3 messages, and can fix all 3 before clicking again.
The rules come from the Player class in chapter 4. The Register window checks nothing itself. It gives each box to the Player class, and shows any error message the class sends back.
When every box is right, the new player is added to the end of `players.txt`. A message says the player is ready, and the window closes.

screens.title: Check that your project is ready, and see the words this chapter uses

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know that your project has everything the Register window needs.
The Register window uses things you made in earlier chapters. Check that each one is in your project.

need: The Files class that finds pictures, in your project (chapter 2).
The Avatars folder inside bin\Debug\Images, with 8 pictures from `summit-ready-files.zip` (chapter 2).
The Player class with its rules, and the exception classes such as SummitException (chapter 4).
The PlayerFile class, with LoadAll and Add for `players.txt` (chapters 3 and 4).
About 2 hours. Your ticks are kept, so you can stop at the end of any screen and come back later.

words: Parent
The control that another control sits on. Each avatar picture has its panel as its Parent.
PictureBox
A control that shows a picture. Each avatar is a PictureBox.
Transparent
`Color.Transparent` lets whatever is behind a control show through it.
avatar
The picture a player chooses to stand for them. Summit Ready has 8 animal avatars.
panel
A control that holds other controls. Each avatar picture sits inside its own panel.
Tag
A spare property on every control, for any value you want to keep with it. Each avatar picture keeps its file name in its Tag.
cast
A type in brackets in front of a value tells C# what the value really is. `(PictureBox)sender` tells C# that `sender` is a picture.
colour from red, green and blue
`Color.FromArgb(242, 183, 5)` mixes a colour from red, green and blue. Each number is from 0 to 255.
lightning bolt
The button at the top of the Properties window that shows a control's events in place of its properties.
Load
Load is what happens a moment before a form's window first appears. Code you put in it runs once.
blocks.intro: You do not need to learn these words now. Where you first meet each one in the chapter, it has a dotted line under it. Hover over it or tap it to see what it means.

screens.title: Type the fields, and the Load method that shows the 8 pictures

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, the 8 avatar pictures appear when frmRegister opens.
frmRegister needs 3 fields. A field is a value that the whole window keeps. They sit at the top of the class, outside every method.

code.title: The 3 fields of frmRegister
code.text:
public string NewUsername = "";    // read by frmLogin afterwards
private string chosenAvatar = "";  // the avatar file, once clicked
private PictureBox[] pictures;     // the eight avatar pictures
partLines: NewUsername
`NewUsername` stays empty until the code creates a player. It is `public`, so the Log in window can read it in chapter 6 and fill in the new username.
chosenAvatar
`chosenAvatar` holds the file name of the avatar the player clicked. It is empty until they click one.
pictures
`pictures` is an array, a numbered list, of the 8 avatar pictures. It lets one loop, a block that repeats, deal with all 8.

screens.title: Type Avatar_Click, which puts a gold frame round the clicked picture

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, clicking any avatar picture gives it a gold frame and remembers the choice.
All 8 pictures run the same method when they are clicked. `sender` is the picture that was clicked, so one method works for every picture.
Each picture sits inside a panel, so the picture's `Parent` is its panel. Changing the panel's `BackColor`, its background colour, changes the frame round the picture.

code.title: Avatar_Click
partLines: Which picture was clicked
`(PictureBox)sender` is a [[cast|6]]. It tells C# that `sender` is a picture, so `clicked` can use the picture's properties.
Take every frame away
The loop makes every panel see-through, so no picture has a gold frame.
Frame the clicked picture

The clicked picture's panel turns gold, made from red 242, green 183 and blue 5. `chosenAvatar` keeps the picture's file name from its Tag. The avatar message is emptied, because the player has now chosen.

screens.title: Add the password and avatar checks to btnCreate_Click

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, **Create my player** checks the password, the password typed again and the avatar.

The other 3 checks have the same shape as the username check. So the copy below holds the whole of btnCreate_Click so far, with gaps. You replace the start you typed, then type the lines that are new.
The password typed again needs 2 `catch` blocks. When the two passwords are different, both boxes are emptied so the player types both again. A blank box only gets its message.
`PasswordMismatchException` is a narrower kind of `SummitException`, which catches every error of that sort. So its `catch` must come first. C# uses the first `catch` that fits.

code.title: btnCreate_Click: the password and avatar checks
code.why: The username check, and the `try` and `catch` lines round each check, are the same as the lines you typed on the last screen. So they come in the copy, and you type the lines that are new.
partLines: The username, as before
This is the start of btnCreate_Click that you typed on the last screen.
Try the password
Setting `Password` runs the password rules in the Player class. A broken rule shows its message under the Password box.
Compare the two passwords
`CheckPasswordsMatch` from chapter 4 throws an exception if the second box is blank, or if the two passwords are different.
Different passwords
The message goes under the second box, and both password boxes are emptied.
A blank second box
Any other exception means the second box is blank. Its message goes under the second box.
The avatar
Setting `Avatar` throws an exception if `chosenAvatar` is still empty, because no picture was clicked. The message goes under the pictures.

screens.title: Finish btnCreate_Click, which saves the new player

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, **Create my player** adds a good player to `players.txt`.
If any check failed, `return` stops the method, so nothing is saved. Otherwise PlayerFile.Add from chapter 4 adds the player to `players.txt`.

code.title: btnCreate_Click: save the player
partLines: Stop if anything is wrong
`!allRight` means that allRight is false. Every message is already showing, so the method stops.
Add the player
`PlayerFile.Add` throws PlayerExistsException if the username is taken already. Then the message goes under the Username box, and `return` stops the method.
Say so and close
`NewUsername` keeps the new username for the Log in window. A MessageBox says the player is ready. `this.Close()` closes the Register window.

glossary: Parent
The control that another control sits on. Each avatar picture has its panel as its Parent.
PictureBox
A control that shows a picture. Each avatar is a PictureBox.
Transparent
`Color.Transparent` lets whatever is behind a control show through it.
avatar
The picture a player chooses to stand for them. Summit Ready has 8 animal avatars.
panel
A control that holds other controls. Each avatar picture sits inside its own panel.
Tag
A spare property on every control, for any value you want to keep with it. Each avatar picture keeps its file name in its Tag.
cast
A type in brackets in front of a value tells C# what the value really is. `(PictureBox)sender` tells C# that `sender` is a picture.
colour from red, green and blue
`Color.FromArgb(242, 183, 5)` mixes a colour from red, green and blue. Each number is from 0 to 255.
lightning bolt
The button at the top of the Properties window that shows a control's events in place of its properties.
Load
Load is what happens a moment before a form's window first appears. Code you put in it runs once.
